messages:
anita: thinking aloud: proposal for a lightweight "probe+lease" admission model for private/VPC installs as an alternative to a full sidecar. goals: minimal operator footprint, dynamic capability discovery, bounded trust window.

marc: high level ok. what's the exact difference vs manifest+probe?

anita: manifest+probe = install manifest (static) + runtime probe (dynamic). probe+lease flips some responsibility: control-plane issues short-lived signed leases after validating a probe. runtime accepts leases instead of maintaining long-lived credentials. lease = admission token, TTL short (30-120s).

samir: why leases help ops?

anita: ops wins: no long-lived control-plane credentials stored on runtime, easier rotation, simpler revocation. routing decisions are based on capability vector included in lease payload. runtime enforces per-request tenant auth still.

yuki: security: how to prevent replay/exfil?

anita: options: nonce + single-use markers, bind lease to client TLS cert (mTLS), or bind to source IP when available. default: short TTL + optional single-use. require signed lease (JWS) with kid pointing to control-plane KMS.

marc: signing key ops: do customers provide their own KMS or do we sign centrally?

samir: recommend flexible: (1) hosted/private with customer-managed KMS -> sign leases with customer key; (2) otherwise control-plane signs and runtime verifies via our root. document both flows.

anita: sample flow bullet list: control-plane -> probes runtime (GET /v1/runtime/probe) -> runtime returns capabilities + probe-challenge -> control-plane verifies connectivity/policy -> control-plane issues signed lease POST /v1/leases -> runtime accepts lease and stores ephemeral lease metadata.

yuki: metrics/observability: runtime emits probe.last_seen, lease.issued, lease.accepted, lease.rejected. control-plane emits lease.sign.fail, lease.verify.fail. label with tenant_hmac + capability_fingerprint. avoid plaintext tenant ids.

anita: sample probe response (illustrative):
```http
GET /v1/runtime/probe HTTP/1.1
Host: runtime.mgmt.local
Authorization: Bearer mgmt-token

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "capabilities": ["streaming","kv-cache:v2","gpu-quant:bf16"],
  "probe_challenge": "c7a9...",
  "probe_ts": "2026-03-08T12:00:00Z"
}
```

anita: control-plane verifies the challenge, checks tenant policy, and then returns lease: `lease_jws` with claims: tenant_hmac, capabilities, issued_at, exp, nonce, kid. runtime verifies signature and TTL before honoring.

marc: canary concerns: without sidecar it's harder to split traffic locally. idea: router can compare lease capability_fingerprint against baseline and route 5% to sidecar-enabled nodes for comparison. we should emit capability-mismatch alerts when performance delta > threshold.

samir: failure modes: if runtime refuses to accept leases (e.g., misconfigured certs), fallback should be manifest-only routing or route conservatively. document clear operator flags: --require-lease or --accept-manifest-only.

anita: downgrade/upgrade policy: if probe shows capability removed -> control-plane should demote new traffic immediately, keep in-flight for grace_period (configurable, default 30s), then evict. if probe flips back on, require N consecutive successful probes (default 2) before re-enabling optimizations.

yuki: telemetry detail: emit rts.lease.latency (time between probe and lease roundtrip), rts.capability.flip_count, rts.routing.demote_events. correlate spans for probe->lease->request.

marc: audit: leases should be logged to an append-only audit stream with signature_kid and issued_by. make revocation quick: publish a revocation list for lease KID and have runtimes reject leases signed by revoked keys.

ops: operator checklist: (1) expose probe endpoint on management network; (2) provide certs for mTLS if possible; (3) upload install manifest as fallback; (4) opt-in to customer_kms if they want to sign with their key.

anita: corner case: air-gapped installs where control-plane cannot reach runtime. fallback is manifest-only mode; runtime must be able to validate signed manifests on disk and optionally pull short-lived leases via an operator-initiated push (operator runs a CLI that POSTs lease to runtime). document CLI flow.

samir: KMS appendix: lease signing cadence 7d rotation recommended for signing keys; lease key TTLs short. prefer HSM-backed signing for ATTESTED_PROBE flows.

infra-bot: created draft RFC: rfc/probe-lease-admission-2026 in docs repo -> https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/probe-lease-admission-2026

anita: next steps: I'll draft the RFC with sequence diagrams, probe CLI example, manifest fallback CLI, and a compatibility matrix (features: local-prefix-cache, offline-retry, streaming, billing hooks). scheduling sync Fri.

marc: tagging security: @marc please review replay bindings and revocation list design.

samir: +1 on KMS appendix. I'll draft it.

yuki: +1 on telemetry plan. Will add metric names and span examples.

anita: thanks team. calling pattern name "probe+lease" unless someone objects.

marc: no objections. +1.

ops: noted. INF-3030 created to track implementation work.
